newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures pare losses but end mostly lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures pare losses but end mostly lower.

text.p: U.S. debt futures pared losses in afternoon dealings but still ended mostly lower after a lightly traded session.
Signs from retailers that Christmas sales may be strong after the key Thanksgiving holiday weekend fueled selling pressure in early dealings, traders said.

In addition, fresh selling emerged when the National Association of Purchasing Mangers' November index showed a larger than expected rise, and construction spending in October grew instead of declined, as forecasters had predicted.
Shortcovering by day traders in afternoon dealings pared losses, however, and most contracts ended steady to slightly lower, traders said.

"Volume was very light," said one eurodollar trader on the floor of the Chicago Mercantile Exchange, who noted that the dollar, after being firm all day, added to gains in early afternoon dealings, which also underpinned the U.S. debt market.
March T-bonds became the lead month today, the first session of the December expiration month.
Traders said most of the rolling from December T-bond positions into March had already occurred last month, and spread activity was subdued.
"There are no problems. The rollover already happened," said one bond futures trader on the floor of the Chicago Board of Trade.

Some analysts expect prices to drift higher, with one analyst setting a target of about 116-12/32 in March bonds by midweek, a level of resistance from mid-February. But others expect profit-taking to weigh on the market ahead of U.S. employment data for November on Friday.

At settlement, March T-bond futures were unchanged at 115-28/32, 10-year T-notes were 3/32 lower at 111-14/32 and muni-bonds were 2/32 lower at 117-28/32. March IMM T-bills were two basis points lower at 95.04 and Eurodollars were one point lower at 94.54. ((--Chicago Derivatives desk (312)408-8750)) ((E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com))
